newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Seven NATO ships sail into Ukrainian port.
newsitem.headline: Seven NATO ships sail into Ukrainian port.

text.p: Seven NATO ships sailed on Sunday into Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odessa on a goodwill visit by the Western military alliance and were greeted by a crowd of mostly friendly locals and a small group of protesters.
"NATO go home!" and "Hands off Ukraine!" read banners held by about 10 demonstrators who described themselves as "patriots".
"They are here to spy," said a man in his 50s who said he had retained his suspicion of the West since serving in the Soviet navy.
But dozens of other locals smiled and waved at the sailors as they arrived on frigates belonging to Britain, the United States, Greece, the Netherlands, Italy and Turkey.
The ships were paying a four-day visit to rest at the port which is home to a largely ethnic Russian population.

Their arrival came on the heels of a summit on Friday in Finland where U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin tried to iron out differences over NATO's plans to expand eastwards, a move Moscow opposes but Ukraine does not.

Ukraine is planning to hold joint naval exercises with NATO countries in August on the Crimean peninsula nearby, which many Russians still consider to be theirs. Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev gave the peninsula to Ukraine as a gift in 1954.
The August Sea Breeze-97 exercises, planned as part of NATO's Partnership for Peace (PfP) programme, have angered Yeltsin and Moscow has declined an offer to participate in them.
The Greek commander of the NATO frigates, Kostas Nikitiadis, exchanged models of ships with the captain aboard Ukraine's Hetman Sagaidachny, named after a 16th century Cossack leader.
Nikitiadis praised Ukraine for being such an active member of the PfP programme and said he did not think Yeltsin's opposition to the August exercises would overshadow his visit.
"I don't think so. We are military people. We cannot decide political questions," he said.
"We are happy to be here," he added.
Relations between Ukraine and Russia have been overshadowed by a row over division of the Black Sea Fleet and the terms of leasing its main base in the Crimean port of Sevastopol.
The signing of a friendship treaty has been blocked for several years and Yeltsin has postponed a visit to Kiev six times.
